## v1.6, or: the port got a new name, a Select menu, and opinions about how you play

First things first: **alttp-zig is now ALTTP-DX**. It stopped being interesting that it's written in Zig a while ago, and "A Link to the Past, but with the extras a re-release would have" fits on the box better. The repo, the app, the window and the title screen all say so now, the title screen with a hand-drawn **DX** in the subtitle's own style, because the game's font has no D and no X and Nintendo did not plan for this.

Your saves, settings, rumble and MSU pack all come with you. The first time the new version starts, it moves your old `alttp-zig` data folder over to `alttp-dx` by itself.

### Achievements

Forty-seven of them: the story, the full shopping list, the side quests nobody reads the dialogue for, and a few challenges for people who think Ganon is too easy with more than three hearts.

- A banner slides down at the top of the screen with the item's own icon and the secret chime when one unlocks.
- They're listed in the start menu and on the last page of the Select menu, with what each one asks for.
- Almost all of them are read from the save data the game already keeps, so nothing about how it plays changes, and an old save gets credit the moment it loads. Load a file that's halfway through and you get one banner with the count instead of a slideshow.
- They count across all three files, kept in `saves/achievements.txt`. Cheats pause them until you're back at the title. Randomizer seeds don't count.

### Select brings the whole menu down

Select used to ask politely in a text box whether you wanted to continue or save and quit. Now it slides down a full menu, the way Start brings down the inventory: **Continue**, **Save and Continue** and **Save and Quit** on the first page, and every setting on the pages after it, L and R to move between them. Select again puts it away. The HUD rides off the bottom with it and comes back when it closes, and it no longer drags BG3's attic into view on the way (the inventory's item names, menu text, and in one sunset corner of Hyrule a wall of "BU").

The game was also crashing if you closed it from any settings page, because it threw the settings away while they were still on screen sliding up. That one's gone.

### Save in a dungeon, wake up in the dungeon

Saving inside a dungeon used to mean continuing at Link's House and walking all the way back to the front door of the place you were just standing in. **Continue From Dungeon**, on by default, starts you at that dungeon's entrance instead, through the same code the game already uses when you fall in battle there. Saves keep the original layout, so a cartridge or any other emulator still loads them and asks the old question.

### Volume that remembers

Volume used to live on Shift+= and Shift+-, which nobody has ever pressed on purpose, and reset to full blast every time the game started. It's a slider on the Sound page now, 0 to 100, saved like every other setting, and it changes the sound as you move it. Music, sound effects, MSU tracks and randomizer seeds all listen to it.

### Import MSU-1

Installing a pack used to mean renaming every track to `alttp_msu-<n>.pcm` by hand. With MSU audio on, the start menu has **Import MSU-1**: drop a folder or a `.zip` on the window, or browse for one. It finds the tracks by number whatever the pack calls them, ignores the readme and the `__MACOSX` folder, checks every track against its CRC, and replaces the pack that was there. Zip64 too, for the packs that cheerfully blow past 4 GB.

### A start menu that explains itself

The start menu got a new coat of paint and learned to explain itself: press Y or I on any setting and it tells you what that setting does. It also has an Achievements screen now.

### Widescreen keeps getting wider

- **The Master Sword's grove** grows its canopy out into the margins instead of showing a green box.
- **The river under the Hyrule Castle bridge** shares a screen with the grove, which the widescreen code found out by planting a forest in a river cave. It has margins of its own now: flat cliff walls, open water, and a wave line that matches on both sides.

### Smaller things

- The mouse cursor hides after two seconds of sitting still in a window, and comes back when you move it.
- The **Nightly** release is a rolling build of whatever's newest, rebuilt overnight when something's changed, for people who like their Hyrule slightly undercooked. The numbered releases are still the ones to play.
- The Nix flake builds with Zig 0.17, thanks to adamzwakk.

### Getting it running

1. Download the game for your system, and the tools if you want them.
2. **macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 11+):** unzip and drag `ALTTP-DX.app` to Applications, then run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/ALTTP-DX.app` (and the same for `zelda3-tools.app`) once. Still not notarized. Still haven't paid Apple $99. You can delete the old `alttp-zig.app`.
3. **Linux (x86_64, glibc 2.35+):** `chmod +x` the AppImage and run it. If it complains about FUSE, install `libfuse2` or `fuse3`, or add `--appimage-extract-and-run`.
4. **Windows (x86_64):** unzip anywhere and run `zelda3.exe` or `zelda3-tools.exe`. SmartScreen will still clutch its pearls: "More info", then "Run anyway".
5. Give the game your US ROM and press Play. For randomizer seeds, generate one on alttpr.com from the Japanese 1.0 ROM (MD5 `03a63945398191337e896e5771f77173`) and drop it on the Randomizer page. No game data is included, as ever.
